title: Four Theories and One Exclusion
intro: The level above gave each theory its verdict. This one gives each verdict the evidence it rests on: which experiment was pointed at, what number came back, and where the paper marks its own case as thin.

chapters.title: The ground rules before any scoring
chapters.body:
The exercise is not framed as a test for consciousness. It is framed as a contribution to [[indicator-properties]], a proposal that an AI system be assessed by measuring properties drawn from several scientific [[theories-of-consciousness]] at once, rather than by picking a winning theory and applying it alone. The properties come from global workspace theory, higher-order theories, attention schema theory, recurrent processing theory and others.

What the paper offers that framework is a structure, not a verdict. Indicators stated as claims about a system's internal organization need something concrete to be checked against, and the [[j-space]] is concrete: the [[jacobian-lens]] reads it, and interventions act on it.

The paper also expects traffic in the other direction. It suspects its results may bear on the theories themselves, by exhibiting a system that displays some of the properties associated with conscious access through mechanisms that differ from the ones those theories posit.

One family of accounts is placed outside the exercise entirely. [[substrate-dependent-theories]] hold that consciousness turns on properties of the brain beyond its functional or computational organization: its physical causal structure, or its biological substrate. The paper's experiments concern the computations a language model performs, not the hardware that performs them.

The consequence is a statement of scope rather than a result. Against those theories the findings are declared not relevant, which is different from negative. Nothing measured here counts for or against them.

The restriction also fixes what the four remaining chapters can be. Every theory checked below ties consciousness to function, so every one of them can be argued with using measurements. Whether functional signatures settle anything about [[phenomenal-consciousness]] is set aside from the paper's first page; what it studies is [[access-consciousness]].

chapters.title: Global workspace theory, with numbers attached
chapters.body:
[[global-workspace-theory]] supplied the design brief, so what is left to say is how each of its claims became a measurement.

Capacity was measured twice. [[j-space-occupancy]] fits the residual stream with a sparse non-negative combination of $K$ lens vectors, and reports the $K$ at which adding one more vector stops beating a same-size set of random directions. That count is near zero through the first third of the layers and plateaus around 25 across the [[workspace-layers]]. Holding $K$ at that median, the variance those directions explain in excess of the random control never exceeds 10%. The [[word-list-experiment]] gives the functional version of the same limit: on an eighty-word list of unrelated words, only about six of the words read so far are present at any comma, and at a single layer the figure is closer to one or two. So [[j-space-capacity]] is small in two senses, in share of the representation and in number of items.

Breadth was measured on the weights. [[mlp-gain]] asks how strongly the next MLP block amplifies a direction, normalized against random directions. Lens vectors reach roughly ten times through the workspace band, while the output directions of individual MLP neurons stay near one ([[fig-32]]). Across positions, [[broadcast-heads]] are the top one percent of workspace-layer heads by relay quality. [[broadcast-head-ablation]] drops readout recall to 0.67 against 0.86 for random heads, and changes the top-1 next token at only 5% of positions. That pairing is what makes [[j-space-broadcast]] a claim about the workspace rather than about the output.

Sharpness was measured on ambiguous inputs. The [[embedding-mixture-experiment]] blends two country embeddings and sweeps the blend; early layers track it smoothly, and from layer 38 the activation sits at one end or the other ([[ignition]]).

The weak point is implementation. Brain broadcast runs on recurrent loops and long-range cortical connections. A forward pass has neither, and the paper does not claim to know whether that matters.
chapters.childScope: Take each global-workspace analog down to its own measurement and controls: [[j-space-capacity]] through [[j-space-occupancy]] and the [[word-list-experiment]] with [[category-displacement]]; [[j-space-broadcast]] through [[mlp-gain]], [[broadcast-heads]], [[label-preservation]] and [[broadcast-head-ablation]]; and [[ignition]] through the [[embedding-mixture-experiment]] and [[bimodal-commitment]].

chapters.title: Higher-order theories and the shape of blindsight
chapters.body:
Self-descriptive readouts do appear in the lens: thinking, focused. The paper does not build on them, because it says they are not the norm. The case it presses for [[higher-order-theories]] is structural, and it rests on the selectivity experiments.

[[blindsight]] is the reference case. Visual information presented to a damaged field still shapes behavior, and a patient can guess the location of a stimulus above chance while reporting no awareness of having seen anything. The higher-order reading is that the information is represented in a first-order sense and not in a higher-order one.

The paper's two selectivity experiments do not have the same shape, and the difference matters for the analogy. In the [[language-passage-tasks]] battery, the passage's language appears in the readouts at comparable rates under all four tasks. A [[lens-coordinate-swap]] exchanging Spanish for French flips the named answer and the flexible inferences, while the continuation stays in Spanish and the spliced foreign sentence is still detected. There the information is in the workspace and causally inert for the routine tasks.

The [[linewrap-task]] is the closer parallel. Asked to keep wrapping lines, the model tracks a running character count, yet number tokens are absent from the lens across the whole prompt, and a swap mapping counts in the forties to the sixties leaves the wrap point where it was. Asked instead how many characters the first line holds, the model answers "46", numbers appear in the lens at twenty positions, and the same swap moves the answer to "65" ([[fig-21]]). [[selectivity]] here is a fact about what enters the workspace, not only about what is used once inside, which is what makes it look like the [[unconscious-processing]] the theory has in mind.

What the paper will not settle is whether the entering representation is higher-order at all, or merely more accessible. Computational variants cast the higher-order state as a pointer that tags a first-order state's reliability. The J-space instead re-encodes the content in words.

chapters.title: Attention schema theory: reports of the operating
chapters.body:
[[attention-schema-theory]] makes a claim about what a report is a report of. A system builds a simplified model of its own attention, and within that model attention is depicted as an act of subjective experience; what is available for report is the model, not the attentional state itself. Applied to a language model, the prediction is that the structure the model reports from carries a description of the operating, not only the thing operated on.

Three results are offered. In the [[experiential-reports]] experiments, the lens contents during stream-of-consciousness narration are dominated by the act itself: thinking appears in the top ten at 58% of position-and-layer slots, thoughts at 23%, feeling at 17%, conscious at 7%. The same words appear substantially less often in the output distribution at those positions, which is the check that they are not simply echoing the text being written. [[j-space-ablation]] over layers 38 to 54 removes the experiential register while the narration stays fluent ([[fig-25]]).

In [[directed-modulation]], the lens carries the instructed content, orange or seven or forty, and beside it [[metacognitive-representations]] naming the act: thinking, imagine, calculate, focused. These sit at earlier layers than the content, as though the operation is represented before its result.

The [[thought-suppression]] experiments go further. Across forty concepts, failure words and damn reach the lens top five on 93% and 82% of trials under the suppression instruction in the post-trained model, against 17% and 30% in the base model, and never at all under a matched positive instruction.

The paper marks its own limits twice. Those suppression words were not shown to be downstream of the failure rather than of the instruction. And none of this is a model of attention as such, which leaves the fit at the edge of what the theory predicts. Widening from attention to self-modeling, the tokens AI, assistant, bot and chat surface at the start of the Assistant's turn independently of the prompt ([[assistant-point-of-view]]).

chapters.title: Recurrent processing theory: depth in place of loops
chapters.body:
[[recurrent-processing-theory]] is the one theory whose verdict looks settled before any measurement. A single feedforward sweep is unconscious however far it propagates, and a representation becomes conscious only once later areas feed back to earlier ones. A [[transformer]] has no recurrence within a forward pass, so on its face the architecture is ruled out.

The paper's reply concerns where the theory came from. Its empirical motivation is timing: conscious perception takes longer than the feedforward sweep alone, and a stimulus must be processed for some minimum duration before it can be reported on. Recurrence is how a brain extends processing past one sweep given fixed anatomy.

Read that way, the operative computational property is serial processing depth, and recurrence is the brain's means of buying it rather than the thing itself.

Depth is what a transformer has instead, and it has it along one of its [[two-time-dimensions]]. The early region identified by the [[layer-bands]] analysis, before the workspace begins, is offered as the functional analog: a representation must pass through some number of stages before it enters the workspace. Whether those stages are stacked in a feedforward net or produced by looping over a shallower one may be an implementation detail rather than a difference in kind. Related work on [[feedforward-emulation-of-recurrence]] supports the exchange, since a feedforward stack can reproduce a recurrent network's computation up to as many steps as it has layers.

Two things sit against this. The reply is an argument, not an experiment, and no measurement in the paper tests it.

And the paper says elsewhere that it does not know why the early band is empty. The content may genuinely require depth to form. Or the lens, whose averaged Jacobian relates each layer to the final layer, may simply fail to read a region that far from the end.
